title: Redox Half-Reaction Balancing Walkthrough
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Step-by-step walkthrough of the half-reaction method for balancing redox equations. Four reactions (three in acidic solution, one in basic solution) are balanced one step at a time, with computed atom and charge counters and a checklist of balancing requirements.

learningObjectives: Carry out each step of the half-reaction method for a redox equation in acidic or basic solution
Verify conservation of mass and charge at each stage and in the final equation
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 4, Topic 4.9: Oxidation-Reduction (Redox) Reactions

controls.label: Select Reaction
controls.description: Chooses one of four redox reactions

controls.label: Next Step
controls.description: Advances one step of the half-reaction method

assumptions: Every line after the skeleton half-reactions is generated by the balancing procedure in code
Atom and charge counters are computed from a species table, not typed in
State symbols are omitted to keep the equations short

keyQuestions: Which counter is each step meant to fix?
Why must the electrons be equal before the half-reactions are added?
Why does adding OH- to both sides keep the equation balanced?
commonMisconceptions: Adding electrons to the more negative side
Balancing atoms but forgetting to check charge
Leaving H+ in an equation for a reaction in basic solution
assessmentOpportunities: Have students write each step on paper before revealing it
